title: Louis Armstrong's broadcasts and Phil Harris in New Orleans
summary: Hirsch recalls Armstrong's 1931 stint with a small band doing broadcasts and talking through the show, compared with Phil Harris at the Blue Room.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Do you remember Armstrong's, uh, State A?

I got, well, uh, he, it was, he had about a six or seven piece orchestra. Uh-huh. Louis, uh, Louis Armstrong, he was Hot Five or Hot Seven or something like that. And they used to do a broadcast from there. And he talked, he talked 90% through the show. Yeah. And it was the same thing with Phil Harris when he was at the Blue Room. Uh-huh. They used to talk and talk and talk and talk. I mean, there was very little music that you could hear. Really. And Phil Harris, oh, they loved Phil in New Orleans. They loved him down here. But, uh, Louis, Louis was, Louis was very well received. He, he was very well liked.
